title: Quyền riêng tư của trẻ · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering restricting parents from sharing identifiable information about their children online. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

vocabulary.meaning: thông tin có thể giúp nhận diện một cá nhân
vocabulary.example: Proposals involving restricting parents from sharing identifiable information about their children online can create difficulties even when their intended benefit is attractive.
vocabulary.note: Dữ liệu nhận diện còn tìm lại được sau khi người đăng quên, còn đứa trẻ không chọn dấu vết đó. Ẩn tên trường và bệnh án phân biệt chia sẻ tin gia đình với phơi lộ thông tin nhạy cảm. Cụm này gọi đúng đối tượng hoặc điều kiện của chính sách; dùng trong ngữ cảnh đã nêu, không thay bằng một từ học thuật chung làm mất nghĩa.

vocabulary.example: Broad restrictions may intrude into private family communication; rules should instead distinguish sensitive public disclosures from low-risk sharing among relatives.

grammar.name: Động từ tình thái chỉ khả năng
grammar.example: Children can acquire a lasting public identity online before they are old enough to consent to it.
grammar.why: Trong câu “Children can acquire a lasting public identity online before they are old enough to consent to it.”, cụm “can” đặt hệ quả ở mức khả năng thay vì khẳng định chắc chắn. Dữ liệu nhận diện còn tìm lại được sau khi người đăng quên, còn đứa trẻ không chọn dấu vết đó. Ẩn tên trường và bệnh án phân biệt chia sẻ tin gia đình với phơi lộ thông tin nhạy cảm.

grammar.name: Đối chiếu hoặc đồng thời với while
grammar.example: Enforcement could then intrude into low-risk communication while offering little guidance about the sensitive information most likely to cause lasting harm.
grammar.why: Trong câu “Enforcement could then intrude into low-risk communication while offering little guidance about the sensitive information most likely to cause lasting harm.”, while nối hai diễn biến hoặc yêu cầu cần xét cùng nhau; ở đây phải giữ cả hai phía để không biến điều kiện giới hạn thành phủ nhận toàn bộ lợi ích. Không suy ra mọi ảnh trẻ đều gây hại ngang nhau hay cha mẹ không được chia sẻ gì. Mức nhận diện, độ nhạy cảm và quy mô người xem thay đổi rủi ro.

paragraphs: Children can acquire a lasting public identity online before they are old enough to consent to it. Broad restrictions may intrude into private family communication; rules should instead distinguish sensitive public disclosures from low-risk sharing among relatives.

Overly broad legal rules could intrude into ordinary family communication. A broad legal ban may fail to distinguish a public disclosure of medical details from an ordinary family message shared privately. Enforcement could then intrude into low-risk communication while offering little guidance about the sensitive information most likely to cause lasting harm. Sharing a family celebration with a limited audience is different from publishing a child's school location or medical history in a searchable public account. Parents may become uncertain about harmless messages to relatives if the law treats every identifying detail as equally dangerous regardless of who can see it. This uncertainty can consume enforcement resources that would be better directed towards public disclosures combining a child's location with highly sensitive personal information.

Guidance and targeted safeguards should focus on sensitive data and substantial harm. Targeted guidance should explain sensitive details and audience settings, with stronger intervention reserved for substantial risks rather than indiscriminate restrictions on family expression. Guidance should show parents how school badges, locations and medical details can identify a child even when a name is omitted, making privacy advice concrete enough to follow. A clear distinction between restricted family communication and searchable public accounts would help parents understand their obligations and allow authorities to concentrate intervention where exposure is most difficult to reverse.
Overall, safeguards should consider identifiability, sensitivity and audience size, protecting children's future autonomy without criminalising ordinary low-risk family communication.
